title: Conveyor Defect Acoustic Emission vs Roller Speed Discriminative Test
mde_rationale: By running a 2x2 matrix (baseline vs defect across two distinct belt speeds of 1.0 m/s and 2.0 m/s), this experiment decouples speed-dependent roller harmonic vibration from defect-induced acoustic emission bursts which must synchronize with the known belt loop circulation time (T = 1.2m / V).
hypothesis: An artificial surface defect generates localized ultrasonic acoustic bursts (>25 kHz) synchronized with belt circulation frequency, distinguishable from roller speed-dependent baseline noise.
alternative_explanation: Measured signal elevation is solely due to roller eccentricity harmonics and motor bearing noise scaling with operating RPM.
equipment: 1.2 m benchtop conveyor testbed with PWM speed controller
Ultrasonic contact acoustic emission sensor (20-100 kHz)
Artificial surface defect clip fixture (1 mm notch)
calibration_steps: 1. Record stationary 0 m/s electrical noise floor for 10 seconds.
2. Verify accelerometer mounting stud torque with calibrated wrench at 2.5 Nm.
3. Apply acoustic couplant and calibrate clamp force to 5.0 N using force gauge.
procedure: 1. Run 30-second baseline recording at 1.0 m/s with no defect.
2. Run 30-second baseline recording at 2.0 m/s with no defect.
3. Stop conveyor and securely mount 1 mm artificial defect clip.
6. Save observation data to data_template.csv and execute analysis.py.
analysis_method: Exploratory descriptive comparison of acoustic peak amplitude and burst periodicity across baseline and defect states at both speeds.

criteria.supports: Acoustic peak amplitude in defect condition exceeds baseline by >=6 dB and burst periodicity matches T = 1.2m / V (1.20s at 1.0 m/s and 0.60s at 2.0 m/s).
criteria.weakens: Acoustic peak amplitude does not exceed baseline noise floor, or scales solely with speed without periodicity matching belt circulation.
criteria.inconclusive: Signal-to-noise ratio is below 6 dB or sensor mounting slips during run.

safety_notes: Operator must maintain safe distance from rotating rollers.
Emergency stop button within arm reach.
Benchtop acrylic shield closed during operation.
assumptions: Artificial defect creates mechanical disturbance comparable to early fatigue micro-crack.
Silicone acoustic couplant remains stable over the 10-minute test sequence.
limitations: Laboratory benchtop results with artificial defect do not represent full multi-month abrasive wear.
High ambient factory noise may require active filtering beyond this screening test.
